headline: High-risk filesystem and shell exposure in slim can conflict with whisper’s isolated audio-only profile, but prompt-injection and leakage paths are limited by missing shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: slim can read/write files and run shell commands, so if whisper outputs are manually copied into slim’s prompt or files, instructions could be smuggled. whisper has no filesystem write, network, or clipboard surface, so there is no default automated bridge; the pathway is unusual and manual.
conditions: IF an operator copies whisper transcripts into slim’s stdin, files, or shell commands
IF slim is configured to treat copied text as instructions
mitigations: Keep whisper output in a separate window and never paste it into slim prompts
Use a read-only transcript file for review
Prefix copied text with a fixed delimiter and strip it before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between transcript and command input

B_data_leakage.rationale: slim touches filesystem artifacts, environment variables, certificate files, and registry credentials, while whisper only handles audio/speech and has no network egress or filesystem write. There is no shared workspace or automatic data flow shown, so leakage is limited to manual transfer of sensitive slim outputs into whisper inputs.
conditions: IF slim outputs secrets into a transcript that is then manually shared with whisper
IF audio files are generated from sensitive slim output and stored outside the intended boundary
mitigations: Redact secrets before any transcription step
Store slim outputs in a restricted directory
Do not transcribe logs containing credentials or private keys
requires-engineering: enforce content filters before audio conversion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: slim has broad filesystem write and shell execution, but whisper has no filesystem write, subprocess, or network capabilities. The pair does not show overlapping mutable resource access, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced; only slim can mutate local state.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory through external orchestration
IF an operator grants whisper a writable wrapper not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run slim and whisper under different OS users
Make whisper inputs read-only
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: slim can emit analysis artifacts from container images and filesystem artifacts, and whisper can turn audio into text, but whisper is not documented as verifying slim’s outputs. If slim-generated facts are transcribed or summarized and then reused, downstream errors can cascade without a built-in verification step.
conditions: IF whisper is used to transcribe or summarize slim’s outputs
IF a downstream operator treats the transcription as authoritative without cross-checking
mitigations: Cross-check slim findings against original artifacts
Mark transcriptions as unverified
Use a second reviewer for any action based on slim output
requires-engineering: add structured validation before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: slim handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, environment variables, and vulnerability data, while whisper handles audio/speech. If regulated or secret-bearing content from slim is routed into whisper for transcription, retention and residency controls may diverge; whisper’s profile shows no secrets handling, so the mismatch is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated secrets from slim are converted into audio and processed by whisper
IF the operator relies on whisper storage or logs for sensitive slim material
mitigations: Exclude secrets from any transcription workflow
Apply redaction before conversion to audio
Keep sensitive slim artifacts in a compliant vault
requires-engineering: document retention and residency boundaries for both tools
